project.name: memory-box
project.productType: Collaborative pixel canvas with notes, photos, build-on links and grounded Find/Ask

design.density: Compact working chrome around a full-viewport canvas

preferredPrimitives: Native buttons with Base UI Tooltip
Original 32px pixel objects for six creation/exploration tools

must: White/pastel pixel identity; actual stored artwork keeps its colors and positions
All six tool labels visible on touch; stationary hit targets at least 44px
No fabricated participants, stories or activity
Open builds show actual current invitations and source-backed contributions; joining does not imply membership, completion or contributor counts
Floating mobile workbench and reply sheets reserve 82px for the dock, scroll within 60dvh/440px and keep actions at least 44px tall
Places derive only from actual stored originals or pixels on the continuous signed sparse plane; pixel-only places survive removal of their last original
Faint stepped pastel geography and dotted travel trails stay beneath authored art; distance labels declutter and hide while reading, painting, placing or using a panel

Authored notes/photos take click and drag priority over overlapping geographic labels on desktop/mobile: transformed authored layer z-index 1, place labels 0, World control 15 and pointer-transparent cursors 11
World map provides actual-content footprints, a current viewport and a keyboard/touch destination list; all three existing zoom levels preserve the current place

Start a place opens an unpublished invitation with explicit placement; substantive or linked drafts and staged paint resume instead, while a pristine empty unlinked draft may be replaced by that explicit action
Mobile World control stays compact and clear of Meet here/presence; the map sheet reserves 82px for the dock, stays within min(68dvh, 490px) and retains visible focus and at least 44px action targets
Cache miniature artwork by content and size, update its viewport on a separate transparent canvas and query the cached sparse index for visible main-layer pixels
Keep real-time, painting, private image upload, build-on and source-backed search behavior
Respect reduced motion; retain keyboard focus and tooltip dismissal
avoid: Marketing slogans or starter counters around the canvas
Idle floating objects, confetti, autoplay or perpetual bounce
Large motion runtimes for simple visual feedback
Invented or empty map destinations, topic-enforced place boundaries or geographic scenery presented as saved contributions
Repainting miniature artwork for camera-only changes or scanning every stored pixel on each main-canvas camera frame

decisions.reason: Extend the canvas-first white/pastel pixel identity across one finite sparse plane. Derive places from actual originals and pixels; use faint stepped pastel contours and dotted geographic trails beneath authored materials, with small original pixel emblems and decluttered distance labels. Explore opens a compact World map with actual pixel/paper/photo footprints, a dashed lilac viewport, wrapping destination names and factual original/open-build metadata. Keep the base miniature cached by content/size and its camera viewport on a separate transparent canvas. Mobile keeps a compact labeled World target clear of Meet here/presence, and a dock-clearing sheet bounded to min(68dvh, 490px) with 44px actions. Start a place suggests empty ground and opens the existing unpublished invitation composer for explicit placement. Resume substantive or linked drafts and staged paint; allow the explicit action to replace a pristine empty unlinked draft. Wander balances eligible occupied places while preferring unseen originals and community originals within that pool. Preserve all three place-centered distance controls, authored positions, visible focus, reduced motion and the main canvas's cached sparse pixel queries. The pilot still fetches full snapshots; no scale claim, topic categories, fabricated activity, new dependency, font or migration follows from this extension.

decisions.direction: Open builds in the shared mosaic
decisions.reason: Extend the existing white/pastel pixel identity with an optional native invitation checkbox below the writing artifact, a lilac Open build badge and actual newest-first invitations ahead of preset patches in Together. Join opens a workbench anchored to the original, with its real author/request/photo, shared-pixel painting, controlled source-linked notes/photos and existing read/share actions. Reuse Pixelify, readable body type, stepped buttons and the bounded mobile sheet; reserve 82px for the floating dock and retain 44px mobile actions. Accepted paint saves capture their actual build source for later attachment. Closed or removed sources show factual status and a return to Together. Joining adds no membership, completion or contributor counts, and the extension adds no library, font, art asset or replacement system.

Actual authored materials remain visible at every zoom; place-preserving presets and unseen-story wandering open a spatial Read/Build on/Next preview. Reuse the source-anchored composer with a bounded mobile sheet, restored draft neighborhood, factual labels and visible explicit threads. Only later received new/updated originals receive a capped 1800ms highlight with static reduced-motion feedback. Preserve compact white/pastel pixel chrome, real cursor/painting layers and stored authorship without fabricated activity, new rendering/motion dependencies or migrations.

User requested smaller non-canvas UI with the cute pixel style throughout. A 56px header, 344px dock and 316px desktop panels use plum ink, butter primary actions and lilac tabs. Short labels use Pixelify; longer text stays readable. Mobile targets remain at least 44px, sheets scroll, dock artwork motion is limited to 2px and 6%, and persistent gesture instructions are removed.

User authorized a more bubbly, tactile, animated refinement of the existing canvas. Distance-based dock artwork motion is adapted from 21st Motion Primitives references; CSS preserves fixed targets and no runtime dependency. Paper tint connects composing to placing. Motion is bounded and user-initiated.
